source.baseline_kind: Local content snapshot of the installed source.

source_oracle.kind: Previously executed fixed-source scenarios and independent call-chain review

runtime.kind: Isolated real App on native Linux amd64, disconnected Docker container, real indexed worker ZIPs, ordinary authenticated App API handlers
observations: The exact four package indexes and ZIP hashes were verified before startup. The installed MergeSiteSwitch opened the native Vuetify form with live priority-ordered numeric site IDs and exposed only the three installed exact peers.
One explicit public save disabled beta, selected alpha for Search and all four peer slots, and left RSS independently set to beta.

The normal SiteUpdated route enabled beta. Search and SiteStatistic appended beta. AutoSignIn and IYUU persisted beta before alpha in their original priority-order reinitializers. The normal SiteDeleted route removed alpha, preserving beta in RSS and the following settings.
All input and site data were synthetic, all writes stayed in the temporary instance, and the stopped container and its bundle were removed.

prior_attempts.observed: The first worker advertised ManagedPublicServices from a serial entry point. Linux installed files and rejected the process during handshake before init. The worker now negotiates the concurrent managed event path.

The fixture expected all peer lists to keep append order. Fixed AutoSignIn and IYUUAutoSeed source initializers filter by priority order and save the filtered list. The final fixture checks separate priority order and append order, with product code unchanged for this correction.

adaptations: The authenticated host save origin replaces Python inspect.stack. Peer fields are allowlisted and updated individually. Only site selections and CustomSites ID/name are projected; complete peer configuration does not cross the worker boundary.

Stable native site IDs are mapped to numeric source IDs. Search and RSS writes require IDs that still resolve to a host site; source SystemConfig permits stale numbers. The site-enable loop ignores unmatched valid numeric IDs. Configured custom IDs preserve their numeric/string type in peer lists.

Exact peer IDs are used. Source BrushFlow is not the installed BrushFlowLanduo. CustomSites, BrushFlow and CrossSeed were absent from the observed installation. Their form and gate behavior is fixed-source-reviewed. SiteStatistic 1.9.7 retains the written statistic_sites field and does not consume it as a filter.

Host registration and process lifetime use the existing managed public-event contract. Reinitialization and job refresh operate on the existing exact peer object. Source authorization level is excluded by user scope.
delivery: Local only. No production state copied or changed. No push, deployment, or published index change.

browser.kind: Chrome on the actual isolated Linux App and unmodified existing Vuetify frontend
browser.observation: Real selection of the second site sent numeric IDs [1,2] in the authenticated PUT. The GET and host store read back the same IDs, both sites became enabled, and unrelated follow settings stayed disabled. No JavaScript exception. The later host delta affects registered event dispatch only.

contended_event.kind: Distinct actual Linux App run with an owned in-flight lifecycle operation and real SiteUpdated from the site management route
contended_event.observation: Before the manager is released the event makes no partial Search selection write. After release the ordinary callback updates Search and SiteStatistic. This validates admission before the worker callback, independent of the already accepted ordinary save, update and deletion run.

review.scope: The independent source reviewer traced form persistence, actual public save origin, typed first removal, exact peer IDs and host call sequence. Evidence hashes matched the source oracle, ZIP, Linux fixture and output. A concurrency review found a possible partial event write, closed by managed operation admission before dispatch and a distinct actual scenario.
